source_neutral.procedure: The object acted on is the enumerated set of deployed changes separating the last known-good checkout deployment, the baseline, from the currently regressed deployment. Changes include code revisions, configuration edits, feature-flag changes, and dependency or infrastructure changes. The regressed configuration consists of the baseline plus all enumerated changes. The procedure tests configurations containing subsets of these changes under a fixed replay workload, repeatedly reduces a configuration that reproduces the defined latency regression, and reports the retained set subject to the test conditions and stopping rules. Preconditions must be checked; the packet does not establish that they hold.
source_neutral.action: Partition the change set into subsets, initially halves. For each subset, build a configuration applying that subset to the baseline and a complementary configuration removing that subset from the regressed deployment. Run the identical fixed replay workload against each candidate with the preset number of repeats, then classify the candidate as fail, pass, or unresolved using the predefined predicate. Retain any reduced configuration that still fails and repeat the reduction on it. If no subset or complement fails, split into more, smaller subsets and repeat. Interleave baseline and full-change control runs throughout to detect test-environment drift. If either control stops producing its expected outcome, suspend reduction and re-establish the test.
source_neutral.observables: The procedure would produce fail, pass, and unresolved outcomes across configurations receiving the same replayed workload, together with per-configuration latency distributions. Relevant signals are which reduced configurations preserve the threshold exceedance; which cease to preserve it; whether the latency gap between a retained configuration and the baseline exceeds the run-to-run spread in repeated control runs; and whether interleaved controls remain stable, with the baseline passing and the full-change configuration failing. Follow-up signals are whether the retained-set versus baseline latency gap persists, grows, or vanishes at different fixed load levels, and whether production latency changes with reversion and reintroduction relative to a concurrent comparison slice. No observations have been made in this packet.
source_neutral.inferential_warrant: If reduction reaches a 1-minimal retained set, that set is a test-relative minimal group of deployed changes sufficient, when applied to the baseline, to reproduce the defined latency exceedance under the replay workload. Each retained member is necessary for reproduction within that set under that test. A single retained change is the candidate accounting for the regression under test. A retained set containing several changes supports the conclusion that they jointly reproduce the regression through an interaction; it does not establish that any member reproduces it alone. Configurations differing in the retained changes receive the same request rate and request mix, so their latency difference in the test cannot be attributed to a difference in load. The multi-load follow-up indicates whether the effect appears across tested load levels or above some level. If performed, production reversion and reintroduction support a causal contribution for the observed traffic slice and period. These conclusions support a bounded causal contribution of the retained changes. They do not establish that production load played no part, that the retained changes explain the entire production regression, or how the changes increase latency.
source_neutral.problem_decomposition: The units are the enumerated deployed changes, subsets formed from them, complementary subsets, candidate configurations, and the baseline and full-change controls. Candidate configurations relate selected changes to the baseline, while subset and complement tests examine which combinations preserve the regression. Finer partitions examine smaller combinations. Retained changes may interact: combinations can fail when their parts pass, and changes can mask one another. Dependencies between changes can prevent separate deployment, as with a schema migration and dependent code. The retained set is assessed as a group and by the effect of reverting each individual member within that group. Repeated runs provide per-configuration distributions and control variation; subsequent comparisons relate retained-set and baseline behavior across fixed load levels and production slices.
source_neutral.next_inquiry: After stopping, rerun the retained set and the baseline at more than one fixed load level to determine whether the latency gap persists, grows, or vanishes with load. Where safe and approved, perform controlled reversion and reintroduction of the retained change or changes on a limited slice of production traffic, comparing it with a concurrent slice without the changes. If the initial fixed-load reproduction condition fails, do not start reduction; proceed to stratified timeline and trace comparison.
source_neutral.limits: Before starting, fix a failure predicate, such as checkout p95 or p99 exceeding the baseline by a prestated margin, and classify a prestated inconclusive band between pass and fail as unresolved. Hold load constant by replaying a recorded or synthetic representative checkout workload at a fixed request rate and request mix in staging or another controlled environment. Under that replay, the baseline must pass and the full-change configuration must fail, each repeated enough times to estimate run-to-run variation. If this reproduction condition fails, reduction does not start. Failure to reproduce is compatible with load or environment dependence but does not establish either. Changes must be applicable or reversible individually or in groups to produce deployable configurations; configurations that cannot build, deploy, or start are unresolved. Suspend reduction if interleaved controls lose their expected outcomes and re-establish the test. Stop when the retained set is 1-minimal: reverting any single retained change makes the regression stop reproducing. Also stop when partitions have reached individual changes and remaining candidates are unresolved, or when the pre-agreed run budget is exhausted; report the retained set as near-minimal in these latter two cases. Interactions and masking can make both halves pass while the whole fails, requiring finer partitions and potentially preventing strong minimization. Latency distributions are noisy; configurations near the threshold can change classification across runs, and too few repeats can misdirect reduction. Coupled changes may be inseparable into deployable configurations, and irreversible changes cannot be removed; these constraints can leave a retained set larger than the true minimal set. Staging can differ from production in data volume, cache state, downstream dependency behavior, hardware, and concurrency. Regressions occurring exclusively in production or with production traffic shape are outside what this replay can reproduce. The fixed workload may omit relevant request types or load levels. Reduction returns one minimal set dependent on partition order; other sufficient subsets may exist and are not enumerated. Testing covers enumerated changes; data growth, third-party latency, traffic-mix changes, and other causes outside that set remain unexamined competing explanations. Results are relative to the chosen metric, margin, and tested load levels. A retained minimal configuration establishes reproducibility under the test, without identifying a unique underlying causal mechanism or establishing that the entire production regression is attributable to the retained changes rather than partly to load.
